title: Naturality in finite coefficients of the constant-section structure map
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a scheme morphism with small pro-etale inverse image $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For every finite commutative ring $B$, let $B_W$ be its coefficient sheaf on $W=T,T'$ and let $c_{g,B}:g^{-1}B_T\to B_{T'}$ be the constant-section map of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. For a homomorphism $\phi:B\to C$ of finite commutative rings let $\phi_W:B_W\to C_W$ be postcomposition on coefficient presheaves followed by sheafification [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Then
$$\phi_{T'}c_{g,B}=c_{g,C}g^{-1}(\phi_T).$$
Equivalently, the adjunct maps $\rho_B:B_T\to g_*B_{T'}$ and $\rho_C:C_T\to g_*C_{T'}$ satisfy $g_*(\phi_{T'})\rho_B=\rho_C\phi_T$.

proof.text: For $W=T,T'$, put $P_{B,W}(U)=\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),B)$ and write $a_{B,W}:P_{B,W}\to B_W$ for the sheafification unit. Postcomposition $P_{\phi,W}(s)=\phi\circ s$ is continuous because $B,C$ are discrete, preserves ring operations pointwise, and commutes with restrictions since $\phi\circ(s\circ h)=(\phi\circ s)\circ h$. By the defining universal property of its sheafified map, $\phi_W a_{B,W}=a_{C,W}P_{\phi,W}$. In particular, writing $\eta_{B,W}(b)$ for a constant section, $\phi_W(\eta_{B,W}(b))=\eta_{C,W}(\phi(b))$ on every object.

source.place: Tag 00WH, proposition-sheafification-adjoint; coefficient presheaves as specified in def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules

proof.text: Use the actual construction of $\rho_B$ and $\rho_C$ in prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map. On an object $U\to T$ and $s\in P_{B,T}(U)$, that construction glues the constant values $b$ over the open fibres of $s$, pulled back to $U\times_TT'$. Applying $\phi_{T'}$ to this glued section gives, on the fibre with value $b$, the constant section $\phi(b)$ by Step 1. Applying $\rho_C$ after $P_{\phi,T}$ gives the identical constant section on each of these same pieces (a fibre of $\phi\circ s$ can be a union of several such pieces). Uniqueness of the gluing gives equality on $s$. Thus the two presheaf maps obtained by precomposing $g_*(\phi_{T'})\rho_B$ and $\rho_C\phi_T$ with $a_{B,T}$ agree. Their target $g_*C_{T'}$ is a sheaf by the stated direct-image functor. The uniqueness clause of sheafification therefore gives $g_*(\phi_{T'})\rho_B=\rho_C\phi_T$ as ring-sheaf morphisms.

source.place: Tag 00WH, proposition-sheafification-adjoint; open-fibre gluing in the statement of prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map

proof.text: Write $L=g^{-1}$, $R=g_*$, with counit $\varepsilon$. The adjoint formula in def-weil-proetale-inverse-image gives $c_{g,B}=\varepsilon_{B_{T'}}L(\rho_B)$. Counit naturality, Step 2 and functoriality give the explicit calculation $$\begin{aligned}\phi_{T'}c_{g,B}&=\varepsilon_{C_{T'}}LR(\phi_{T'})L(\rho_B)\\&=\varepsilon_{C_{T'}}L(R(\phi_{T'})\rho_B)\\&=\varepsilon_{C_{T'}}L(\rho_C\phi_T)=c_{g,C}L(\phi_T).\end{aligned}$$ This is elementary naturality of the counit belonging to the specified adjunction. For the stated equivalence, the adjunct of $\phi_{T'}c_{g,B}$ is $R(\phi_{T'})\rho_B$, by the formula $\alpha\mapsto R(\alpha)\eta$; the adjunct of $c_{g,C}L(\phi_T)$ is $\rho_C\phi_T$, by naturality of the unit $\eta$. Since the adjunction correspondence is a bijection, equality of either pair is equivalent to equality of the other.
